title: Jimmy Noone, Johnny Dodds, Bab Frank and Chicago clubs
summary: Dominique praises Noone and Dodds as clarinet readers, recalls flutist Bab Frank, his Chicago jobs with Noone, and a job with Barney Bigard.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: So, them kind of fellas, I can tell you a lot about them, because I know them, I work with majority of them. Now we couldn't come to Jimmy Noon. I work with Jimmy Noon. My last recording on the deck was, you remember, with Jimmy Noon. Jimmy Noon and everybody. Johnny Dotson. My last recording on the deck. Johnny Dotson and Jimmy Noon. Jimmy Noon's a good musician. Read clarinet parts like nobody's business. I mean clarinet parts. And Johnny Dots could read clarinet parts. Very few clarinet parts you can find read clarinet parts. They'd read upper corner parts the matter. And of course they'd be able to improvise it, you know, jazz it the way they want. But when you put a clarinet part, like in parades and stuff, you got strictly clarinet. You have a lot of... Sometimes you come across 64 notes, 64 notes. You can hear those clarinet parts. Very fast. Similar to flute, yes. And Bab Frank. Great flutist. He was only flutist in New Orleans. And that's what old man Papa Dio had for flutists in that... in that symphony orchestra. Bab Frank. Great flutist. Never could play clarinet. And Jimmy Noon, I worked with Jimmy Noon plenty of times. Worked with him on gigs. I worked with him at the Paradise Cafe. I worked with him at the Apex Club. Paradise Cafe on Indiana 31st. The Apex Club on 31st and Calumet opposite the Sunset Cafe. I know what they all can do. And I played one job with Barney D. Gardner. When I worked with King Oliver.
Barney is your cousin. My cousin.

One job with Barney. He was busy, I was busy. The only one who had that after hour dance, you see. At the Sherman Hotel. I'll never forget that. That's why I worked with Barney. And Albert Dix was too. Wasn't that one learned under Lorenzo Dio. He's in New York. There's two in New York that learned under Dio. Orma Simeone and Albert Dix today. Good clarinet.
